title: fix(daemon): preserve safety refusals during service-start recovery
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared service-start recovery can hide an unsettled native cleanup error or observed ownership refusal behind a later missing-install observation. Setup can then enter installation recovery instead of preserving the safety refusal.

## User Impact

Cleanup and ownership failures remain visible before recovery can choose another lifecycle action. Ordinary failed-start recovery, including missing installation artifacts, remains unchanged. Initial absence, stop/start bootstrapping, repair checks and native post-start failure verification are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing service inspection fallback policy at the shared start owner's catch. No new classifier, helper, error subtype, state or recovery path is introduced. Production:+2lines; existing owner tests:+16net lines. This is a swallowed safety-failure bug exception, not cleanup-floor credit. No public signature, schema, config, protocol, dependency, permission or persisted-format change.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

No speculative guard is removed. Ordinary recovery still reads the service state; canonical cleanup and observed ownership refusal no longer qualify for that fallback. Existing effect authority, native settlement and missing-install behavior remain.

The recovery catch originates in refactor258a214; #116815 later moved it while adding post-start checks, which remain. Human issue #53878 describes normal stop/start with an existing LaunchAgent plist; that bootstrap path remains. No newly verified human cleanup incident is claimed.

## Evidence

- Existing shared-owner disappearance regression is extended to ordinary, canonical-cleanup and ownership-refusal errors. Ordinary missing-install recovery is retained; safety errors must reject with their original identity. No new production seam, duplicated nested-error matrix, timeout, retry, skip, baseline or suppression change.
- Actual CLI and setup consumers were inspected. A broader catch-deletion prototype was withdrawn after setup's installation-recovery contract was identified; it is not part of this diff or credited reduction.
- The original local runtime attempt stopped130 BEFORE assertions during compiled subprocess preparation; no baseline/head runtime pass or live-platform claim. No identical cold retry or broad build. Exact-head hosted CI is required for runtime proof.
- Fresh independent full two-file P0–P2 review with eleven complete unchanged-owner datasets, including setup: scoped-clean0.97, final source verification complete. The earlier withdrawn-prototype review is not reused. Focused standard syntax lint, four-file85ms formatting and whitespace checks passed; source/review hashes match. Two-root targeted types exited2 only for unchanged missing parse5/split MCP declarations and their implicit-any cascade, with no changed-file diagnostic; not a local typecheck pass. No new import-closure/SCC: the policy module was already reached by service-state; public signatures and SDK exports are unchanged. Broad graph/API checks remain hosted proof.
- Mandatory lint-suppression suite completed: 13 passed, 1 failed. The sole failure is the existing extra admission-role test-support suppression (98 received versus 97 expected). Both the support file and assertion are byte-identical to the parent and freshly fetched main; this two-file daemon diff adds no suppression. The baseline is not weakened.
- Exact-head ready CI39054371404 completed successfully. All198 check-runs accounted for:68success/128skip/1neutral/1superseded draft-context cancellation with a successful same-head successor; no failed or unfinished check. All three commit statuses passed. No CI rerun, confirmation push or rebase. Local runtime/type gaps above remain honestly scoped; completed hosted CI supplies the broad proof.

Release-note context: Gateway service-start recovery preserves native cleanup and ownership refusals instead of reporting a missing installation.
